abertura: You get fifteen seconds to prepare and forty-five seconds to speak. That is the shape of the independent speaking task in the TOEFL iBT — and it is also the shape of the minute you get in a meeting.
Mark the three statements that are true of a good forty-five-second answer.

itens.t: It takes a position in the first eight seconds.
It gives the best possible position.
It has two reasons, not four.
It uses the fifteen seconds to decide, not to write.
It ends when the time ends.
It needs an example for every reason.

sec1.rationale: Two of the wrong ones are the same mistake: treating forty-five seconds as a short essay. It is not. It is a position, two reasons and a close — and the close has to arrive before the clock does.

nota.titulo: Why the exam format is in this block
nota.texto: Not as exam practice. You asked for the TOEFL in the first lesson of this course, and this is the most demanding short-presentation genre there is: everything from lessons 3, 4 and 5 is charged at once, under a clock, with no second attempt.

abertura: Choose the better reading for each expression.

itens.t: I would say
alts: I am taking a position, and I am not hedging it away
I am not sure
itens.ok: I am taking a position, and I am not hedging it away

itens.t: mainly for two reasons
alts: I am announcing the shape of what follows
there are more reasons I will not give
itens.ok: I am announcing the shape of what follows

itens.t: To take one example
alts: this is the only example
I am about to make the reason concrete
itens.ok: I am about to make the reason concrete

itens.t: That said
alts: I am conceding, briefly, and moving on
I am changing my position
itens.ok: I am conceding, briefly, and moving on

itens.t: So on balance
alts: I am unsure between the two
I am closing, and the close weighs both
itens.ok: I am closing, and the close weighs both

itens.t: which is why
alts: I am tying the reason to the position
I am adding a new idea
itens.ok: I am tying the reason to the position

nota.texto: Mainly for two reasons costs you one second and tells the listener the whole shape of the next thirty. In forty-five seconds, that second is the best investment available.

abertura: Six sentences from forty-five-second answers. Where does each one belong?

itens.t: "No team understands every risk before shipping."
"So on balance, I would ship early with a plan."
"To take one example, the false-decline rate only appeared in production."
"A long delay has a cost nobody counts."
"I would say launch and correct."
"In my last role we held a release for four months and shipped into a changed market."

nota.titulo: The close is not a summary
nota.texto: “So on balance…” does not repeat the reasons. It re-states the position after having weighed them — which is why it sounds like a decision and a summary sounds like running out of time.

doc.texto: “Some people believe a company should delay a product launch until every risk is understood. Others believe it is better to launch and correct as you go. Which do you agree with? Explain why, using specific reasons and examples.”

abertura: You will hear one answer in class. Mark the three things a good answer does here.

itens.t: Chooses one of the two sides, without arguing for both.
Announces how many reasons are coming.
Mentions the other side, briefly, and keeps its position.
Gives three reasons, to be safe.
Explains the two positions before choosing.
Finishes exactly at forty-five seconds.

sec4.rationale: Explaining both sides before choosing is the single most common way to run out of time. The prompt already explained them; your forty-five seconds are for the choice.

nota.titulo: The concession is worth four seconds
nota.texto: Mentioning the other side and keeping your position is the move from lesson 5, at speed. It costs four seconds and it is what separates an answer that sounds decided from one that sounds like it never heard the objection.

abertura: Complete each move so that the forty-five seconds hold together.

itens.t: I would say
alts: that both sides have a point
it depends on the company
launch and correct, mainly for two reasons
itens.ok: launch and correct, mainly for two reasons

itens.t: First,
alts: there are several considerations
no team understands every risk before shipping
I have worked in technology for many years
itens.ok: no team understands every risk before shipping

itens.t: To take one example,
alts: in my last role we held a release for four months
risk is always present
this happens a lot
itens.ok: in my last role we held a release for four months

itens.t: That said,
alts: I would change my answer for a safety-critical system
I am not sure about this
the other side is also correct
itens.ok: I would change my answer for a safety-critical system

itens.t: So on balance,
alts: there are arguments both ways
I would ship early with a plan to correct
it is a difficult question
itens.ok: I would ship early with a plan to correct

nota.titulo: Every rejected option is a way of not answering
nota.texto: “It depends”, “there are arguments both ways”, “it is a difficult question” — all true, all polite, and all of them spend seconds without taking a position. In forty-five seconds, not choosing is the answer, and it is the wrong one.

abertura: Complete the answer. Every gap is one of the six expressions from activity 2.
Then say it out loud once, with a clock. It should land between forty and forty-five seconds.
itens: {I would say|130px} we should hold the launch, {mainly for two reasons|200px}.
First, an unexplainable decision is a decision we cannot defend, {which is why|140px} the regulator asked for it.
Second, the fix is six weeks. {To take one example|180px}, the last pipeline rebuild took five.
{That said|110px}, a delay has its own cost and I am not pretending otherwise.
{So on balance|140px}, six weeks now is cheaper than a license review later.

nota.texto: In class you will say this against a clock, and then again on a prompt you have not seen. Writing it now is what makes the first forty-five seconds about delivery instead of about deciding.

at6.prompt: Before you hear the model: mark the two things your own attempt did.

itens.t: Took a position in the first eight seconds.
Announced how many reasons were coming.
Explained both sides before choosing.
Ran out of time before the close.
Used an example from my own work.

at6.rationale: This is your own attempt, not a right answer. Mark it honestly — the point is to hear the model against what you actually did, not against what you meant to do.

itens.t: "rather than wait for a certainty that never arrives"
"No team ever understands every risk before shipping."
"A long delay has its own cost, and nobody counts it."
"I would say launch and correct."
"So on balance, I would ship early with a plan to correct."
"You find the real ones in production, from real users."

nota.texto: Position, two reasons with one example, a concession and a close. That is the whole architecture, it fits in forty-five seconds, and it is the same architecture as your three minutes in lesson 3 — only faster.

abertura: The shape, and the words that hold it together.

tabela: I would say… , mainly for two reasons.

abertura: Record three answers, if you would like to. Fifteen seconds to prepare, forty-five to speak.

callout.texto:
1. Should companies be required to explain how their AI systems make decisions?
2. Is it better to be managed by someone who knows your work, or by someone who does not?
3. Should a leader admit uncertainty in front of a large team?

abertura: Write the five-move shape for one of the three prompts above, then say it against a clock.

callout.texto: If it runs long, the reason is almost always the same: you explained the two sides before choosing. The prompt already did that.
